18.04.2023, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 B.A.No.2773/23 2
 Order
This is an application filed u/s 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure seeking pre-arrest bail.
2. Petitioners are the accused in Crime No.2958 of 2022 of Kottarakkara Police Station.
The 1st
petitioner i
s the husband of the de facto complainant.
The 2 nd petitioner is the mother of the 1 st petitioner.

Offences alleged against the petitioners are under Sections 498A and 323 IPC.
3.
Marriage between the 1st petitioner and the de facto complainant was solemnized on 26.09.2022 and thereafter they were residing at the house of the petitioners.
It is alleged that, during her stay Ajayakumar vs The State Of Kerala Represented By The ...

sentences.text:

1
with the petitioners, they ill-treated the de facto complainant physically and mentally, by making constant demands for more gold and money.
Complaint was submitted in such circumstances and this application for bail is submitted by the petitioner seeking anticipatory bail as they apprehend arrest.
4. Heard Sri.M.Anuroop, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.C.N.Prabhakaran, learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are implicated in the case with false allegations.
According to them, complaint was submitted by the de facto complainant due to certain matrimonial disputes between the 1 st petitioner and the de facto complainant.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioners are prepared to abide by any of the conditions imposed by this Court and willing to co-operate with the investigation.
6. On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor would oppose the aforesaid contention, pointing out that, there are allegations against the petitioners and the matter is being investigated.
I have gone through the records and heard the contentions of both sides.
Materials placed before me do not indicate any serious allegations against the petitioners.
There are certain matrimonial disputes between the parties.

Considering the nature of allegations and the relationship between the parties,
I am of the view that, the interest of justice would be served, if the cooperation of the petitioners with the investigation is ensured.

7. In the above circumstances, this application is disposed of with the following directions:
(i) The petitioners shall surrender before the Investigating officer, within a period of two weeks from today, for subjecting themselves to interrogation.

(ii) After interrogation, the petitioners shall be released on bail, on the very same day of surrender upon the petitioners executing a bond for Rs 1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) each with two sureties each for the like sum, to the satisfaction of the investigating officer (iii) The petitioners shall fully co-operate with the investigation, including subjecting themselves to the deemed police custody for the purpose of recovery, if any, as and when demanded.
(iv) The petitioners shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m on every Wednesday until further orders.
(v) The petitioners shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required by him.
(vi) The petitioners shall not commit any offence of similar nature while on bail.

2 (vii) The petitioners shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions, the jurisdictional Magistrate/Court shall be empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law.
